paper_metadata.title: Realization of a quantum walk in momentum space with a Bose-Einstein condensate

summary: The paper demonstrates a discrete-time quantum walk in momentum space using a Bose-Einstein condensate of about 70,000 87Rb atoms, with a microwave coin and optical-lattice ratchet shift. The walk is shown up to 20 steps, with biased-coin and biased-ratchet variants, reversal after 8+8 steps, and a quantum-to-classical transition as phase randomness increases from 0% to 100%; no practical computational advantage is established.

experiments.description: Discrete-time quantum walk in momentum space using a Bose-Einstein condensate of 87Rb atoms, with a microwave coin and optical-lattice ratchet shift; includes standard walk, biased walk, walk reversal, and quantum-to-classical transition under phase noise.

algorithm.variant: discrete-time quantum walk in momentum space with quantum ratchet shift

hyperparameters.coin_pulse: pi/2 microwave pulse for symmetric walk

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initial state prepared as |1> then Bragg pulse creates (|n=0> + e^{i0}|n=1>)/sqrt(2); symmetric coin uses pi/2 MW pulse

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Two internal hyperfine states of 87Rb act as the coin; momentum states form the walk space. Conditional momentum shifts are implemented by a quantum ratchet in an optical lattice.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Demonstrate and control discrete-time quantum walk dynamics in momentum space; observe ballistic spreading, biasing, reversal, and decoherence to classical diffusion.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Not applicable; control via coin bias, ratchet asymmetry, and phase noise.

problem_instance.description: Quantum walk of ultracold 87Rb atoms in momentum space with internal-state coin; experiments include standard symmetric walk, biased coin walk, biased ratchet walk, reversed walk, and noisy walk.

dataset_specification.description: 87Rb Bose-Einstein condensate; F=1,mF=0 and F=2,mF=0 hyperfine states; standing-wave optical lattice at 780 nm; Talbot time 103 us

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: BEC prepared by evaporative cooling in optical dipole trap; Bragg pulse used to prepare initial momentum superposition; time-of-flight imaging used to read out momentum distribution
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Comparison of experimental momentum distributions with numerical simulations; multiple configurations shown in figures; no explicit run count reported

noise_model.noise_type: decoherence and phase noise; thermal cloud; spontaneous emission

implementation_details.classical_solver: numerical simulation of effective one-particle theory
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: BEC preparation; Bragg pulse; microwave pulse shaping; optical lattice pulse timing
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Absorption imaging after ~10 ms time of flight; momentum distribution extracted from images

speedup_claims.conditions: ideal quantum walk with coherent unitary evolution
speedup_claims.caveats: Described as a qualitative scaling advantage; no explicit runtime speedup factor is reported.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Not characterized asymptotically; paper notes quantum walks can be building blocks for universal quantum computing and searches of marked momentum states

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not applicable; the paper demonstrates a physical quantum walk on ultracold atoms with up to 20 steps, but does not benchmark a computational task against a classical algorithm in a way that establishes advantage.
limiting_factors: Classical comparison is only to random-walk scaling and numerical simulation
Physical implementation is not a gate-model algorithm

notes: hardware.type inferred as real_qpu_neutral_atom because the experiment uses neutral 87Rb atoms in a Bose-Einstein condensate with optical lattice and microwave control; no gate-based quantum processor is used.
num_qubits inferred as 2 because the coin degree of freedom is encoded in two internal hyperfine states; the walk space is momentum states, not qubits.
circuit_depth not reported because the paper describes physical pulse sequences rather than a gate-model circuit depth.
The paper reports ballistic spreading and reversibility of a discrete-time quantum walk, but not a practical quantum advantage over classical computation.
